segments: of Badr al-Din.
And Badr al-Din remained with a few men in the center,
and he was not able to withstand the main force of the Lord of Arbil.
And Badr al-Din fled before Muzaffar al-Din,
and with swift feet he came and crossed the Tigris to Mosul.
And he did not stop,
but went and encamped in the city of Balad,
so that he might gather forces again.
And Muzaffar al-Din pursued after him and came and encamped behind the hill of the fortress of Nineveh,
and he stayed there for three days.
And when he heard that Badr al-Din was preparing to attack him by night,
he left and went to Arbil.
And during his crossing at Nineveh he harmed no one,
except only that some of the Shahrazuris who were with him snatched a young girl, a newly married bride, from the village of Beth Sahraye.
And her masters were enraged and rescued the girl,
and they also killed some of the Kurdish men.
And Muzaffar al-Din heard {OCR?} and was exceedingly angry,
because it was told to him:
"Those peasants insulted you while shouting,
'Long live the golden sceptre, Badr al-Din!'"
And he sent a force against that village,
and they attacked those innocent villagers who had fortified themselves in the church,
and they killed about three hundred souls of them and left.
And when they crossed through Bartelle,
they cut off the hand of a certain young man with a sword.
And after these things, envoys were sent from one to the other,
and peace was made.
And in that same year,
those who were in the fortress of Kawashi, when they saw the rest of the fortresses that had been surrendered to Imad al-Din Zangi,
they also sent to him and surrendered Kawashi to him,
and they drove out the house of Badr al-Din from there.
And when Badr al-Din saw that Muzaffar al-Din was not ceasing from his hostility,
and was not resting from inciting Zangi to provoke war with him,
he sent to al-Malik al-Ashraf and asked him to come in person to his aid,
and to reprove the Lord of Arbil.
Now al-Ashraf, because his adversaries were many at that time—
Sultan Kaykaus of the Rhomaeans,
along with the Lord of Amid and Hisn Kayfa,
and the Lord of Mardin,
and also the Emir Bar Mashtub,
and the Emir Izz al-Din al-Hamidi,
had rebelled against him—
was not able to come to the aid of Badr al-Din,
except after some time.
And in that same year,
